topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I stood there, the ground beneath my feet where once roots spread wide and deep. The stump, a brutal circle of life arrested, lay under my gaze. I recall the sapling, a fragile sprout, now a story of time abruptly ended. My hands, which once held it gently, curled involuntarily. Each ring inside that harsh boundary held secrets of sun and rain, whispers of childhood. I trace them, feeling the grain, the texture of a life parallel to my own, now silenced. The air seems different here, stripped of something. A part of me, perhaps. The quiet around is heavy, weighing more than the silence of a forest. I stand, not just mourning a tree, but a chapter closed, its pages now pale stumps in the memory.
